newsitem.title: USA: Kmart to spend $750 mln on new store concept.
newsitem.headline: Kmart to spend $750 mln on new store concept.

text.p: Kmart Corp Chief Executive Officer Floyd Hall said Wednesday the retailer plans to spend about $750 million through 1999 to convert nearly all of its traditional Kmart stores into a new concept called "Big Kmart."
Kmart has more than 2,000 traditional Kmart stores in the U.S., in addition to 97 other Super Kmart Centers.

Hall said the company plans to open seven traditional stores and three Super Kmart Centers in 1997 and concentrate its efforts on opening 35 new Big Kmart stores and 15 to 18 Super Kmart Centers in 1998.

The Big Kmart concept offers much of the same merchandise found in a traditional 60,000 to 80,000 square foot Kmart store, although the products are displayed in wider aisles and a new layout that is designed to help shoppers save time and money.
It has been under development for the last 18 months under the name "high frequency" concept.

However, Big Kmarts will also include a new Pantry section that offers some food items such as milk and eggs. Super Kmart Centers, which measure about 180,000 square feet, offer full grocery sections.

Hall, who attended the unveiling of the Big Kmart name in Chicago, told reporters the company continues to talk to potential buyers of its Builders Square home improvement stores. An agreement to sell the stores to Waban Inc fell through ealier this month.
Kmart has been discussing a sale with investors interested in buying the chain, as well as home improvement companies that may want to merge it into their existing operations.
Hall said Kmart is looking to exit Builders Square by the end of 1997.
"We think this is realistic," he said.
In interview with Reuters, Hall said the company is also in discussions to sell its Kmart Canada unit.
"Quite frankly, I'm optimistic somebody will make us an offer in Canada that we'll find acceptable," said Hall, adding he expects an offer to be made this year.
Kmart has been considering a sale of its Canadian division since the fall of 1995.
Hall also said he hopes Kmart can achieve an investment grade rating on its debt by 1998.
"I would think that sometime in 1998 would be realistic," he said, "but I might be a little optimistic on that."

The company said in March it had completed repayment of a $1.2 billion loan taken out in 1996 as part of a refinancing. Officials have said the repayment of the term loan was a necessary step toward improving its credit rating, which was cut below investment grade at the end of 1995.
